summary: Pasadena sits at the base of the San Gabriel Mountains, and on a clear winter morning the snowcapped peaks loom so close above Old Town's rooftops that the city feels more like a mountain-valley outpost than part of the Los Angeles basin — yet the 210 and 110 freeways, plus a Gold Line Metro station, plug it directly into downtown LA roughly twelve miles southwest. This is genuinely a job center, not a bedroom community: Caltech, JPL (NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory), Huntington Memorial Hospital, and a thick cluster of engineering and research firms mean a household earning the $104K median income can plausibly work within city limits. Affording a home is another matter — a median price above $1 million puts the price-to-income ratio past ten, so even well-compensated renters at $2,218 a month may stay renters a long time. The tradeoff buys a walkable urban core along Colorado Boulevard with genuine sit-down restaurants, independent coffee shops, and a weekly farmers' market, plus direct trail access into the Angeles National Forest foothills. With 9.4 hours of daily sunshine and an average high of 77°F, outdoor life is nearly year-round, though summer days in this inland valley run considerably hotter than coastal LA. Pasadena functions as a small city that happens to be embedded inside a giant one — with its own Rose Bowl, its own research economy, and its own price of admission.
